source: User-supplied Bing Webmaster Tools dashboard screenshots captured 2026-09-19. These are aggregate dashboard readings, not page-level exports.
measurementBoundary: AI citations and traditional search performance are separate observational surfaces. Citations are not clicks, rankings, revenue, conversions, or proof that a search change caused an outcome.
objective: Convert proven answer-engine authority into qualified organic search impressions and clicks without sacrificing scientific, safety, canonical, accessibility, or provenance standards.
priorityOrder: Pages with meaningful impressions and CTR materially below the expected curve at their observed position.
Pages in positions 4-15 with meaningful impressions, especially when they are already proven AI-citation assets.
High-citation pages with weak search exposure only when query-intent, internal-link, metadata, or content gaps are evidenced by page/query exports.
Net-new content only for a genuinely distinct query intent after cannibalization and canonical-owner checks.
Pure citation-count growth is secondary unless it also protects a winner or closes an evidence/safety gap.
guardrails: Never use citation count alone to justify a title/H1/canonical rewrite.
Never let CTR optimization overstate efficacy, certainty, safety, dosage, or comparative superiority.
Preserve winning/running metadata experiments until their measurement window closes.
Prefer reversible metadata/internal-link experiments before broad content rewrites on proven citation winners.
Do not manufacture page-level conclusions from aggregate dashboard totals.

searchFreshnessPolicy.rule: Page-level search observations must carry a dated observation end and be no more than 10 days old. Missing, invalid, future-dated, or stale search observations fail closed to a waiting state.

searchPerformance.windowNote: Aggregate dashboard screenshot; exact search date selector was not visible in the supplied image.
